S6a-architecture-01.survivingClaim: Delta over CD-025's surviving claim, narrowed on three counts. (1) The simulation write ORDER diverges one-sidedly: write_simulation_results emits simulation/metadata.json with status complete plus the empty simulation/_SUCCESS sentinel (results_writer.rs:151-154) and runs FIRST on the CLI at outputs.rs:186 although every one of its inputs is already built by simulation.rs:220-249, so a failure in the three later writes leaves the completion sentinel beside a missing paths.parquet or scenario_summary.parquet; the bindings' opposite placement at run.rs:855 is data-forced, not a free choice. (3) A second verbatim copied transform beyond the scenario-summary reshape already in the prior claim: the eight-argument delta_to_stats_row call with its five None slots at outputs.rs:197-206 and run.rs:824-833. NOT surviving: that the two orders are exact reversals (CLI results/stats/paths/summary against bindings paths/summary/stats/results is not a reversal); that the bindings' ordering is free (run.rs:760-762 pins paths before finalize, and sim_out is incomplete until :767, :803 and :807); and a cobre-io home for the delta_to_stats_row fold, whose input SolverStatsDelta and helper are cobre-sddp-owned (outputs.rs:29, :35), so that piece of the fix shape is an owner call, not a station direction.
S6a-architecture-01.argument: The divergence is real but the candidate overstates it in two ways and understates it in one. Overstatement 1: the orders are NOT exact reversals. The CLI emits results, stats, paths, summary (outputs.rs:186, :209, :212, :221); the bindings emit paths, summary, stats, results (run.rs:763, :799, :836, :855). An exact reversal of the CLI would be summary, paths, stats, results, so two of four positions differ from a reversal; only the endpoints are swapped. Overstatement 2: the bindings' order is not a free choice, it is data-forced and the code says so. run.rs:760-762 states that the writer already holds every scenario's node-path rows and that write_paths runs before finalize consumes the writer, and sim_writer.finalize(sim_time_ms) at :766 is what produces sim_out, which is then still incomplete until failed (:767), cost (:803) and solve_stats (:807) are populated, so write_simulation_results cannot move earlier on that path. Understatement: the CLI side IS free and the consequence is sharper than two different partial trees. write_sim_outputs_on_root (simulation.rs:220-249) hands write_simulation_outputs a fully built merged_sim_output plus all four data payloads, so nothing inside outputs.rs:178 constrains the order; and write_simulation_results is not a header manifest, it writes simulation/metadata.json with status complete and the empty simulation/_SUCCESS sentinel (results_writer.rs:151-154). Running it first therefore plants the completion sentinel before paths.parquet (simulation_writer.rs:1196-1200) and scenario_summary.parquet (simulation_writer.rs:1245-1249) exist, so a mid-write failure on the CLI leaves _SUCCESS and status complete beside an incomplete tree, while the bindings' data-forced order happens to get the sentinel semantics right. The absent peer symbol also checks out and is an asymmetry inside the bindings themselves: run.rs declares write_training_artifacts at :532 as the training peer, but the simulation writes sit inline in run_simulation_phase_py (:696) interleaved with aggregation, so there is no simulation unit to align. The second copied transform checks out verbatim (the eight-argument delta_to_stats_row with five None slots at outputs.rs:197-206 and run.rs:824-833) and is new over the prior claim, which named only the scenario-summary reshape; but its home is NOT the L2 entry point, because delta_to_stats_row and SolverStatsDelta are cobre-sddp types (imported at outputs.rs:29 and :35), so folding that mapping into cobre-io would make L2 depend on an engine crate. I therefore keep the duplication as observed fact and strip the L2 destination for it, leaving the attacker's C6 as the owner question. byteNeutral asserted for the residue I confirm: reordering the CLI's four calls so the sentinel lands last changes no emitted byte on a successful run, since write_paths sorts internally (simulation_writer.rs:1172), write_scenario_summary writes rows verbatim (:1227-1231) and write_simulation_results serializes an already-populated SimulationOutput, so the determinism parity golden, the file-set parity test, the 18-shared-name gate and the validate --json object all hold unchanged. Both refinement arms land inside that same family: SOLVER_ERROR (errors.rs:134-136) and SIMULATION_ERROR (errors.rs:143-145) are both BuiltinBase::Runtime, so the fallthrough at errors.rs:249 is not an unowned default but the family-correct base of the two refinements, which exist only to attach structured stage/iteration/scenario ints and to pick the simulation sibling class. The candidate's 'two classification tables' framing does not hold, because the target vocabularies are not comparable in the way the argument needs: CliError::exit_code (crates/cobre-cli/src/error.rs:107-112) returns four disjoint integers for which no correct default exists, so exhaustiveness is the only mechanism that can force a choice, whereas the Python targets form a dual-base subclass lattice in which a missed refinement degrades specificity without becoming wrong and stays catchable by except RuntimeError and by except CobreError. The fallthrough is regression-pinned rather than prose-only: convert_error_non_infeasible_arms at errors.rs:427 drives it with SddpError::Validation, the exact variant the candidate calls out, and asserts SOLVER_ERROR with the three attributes None; that Rust test population is CI-visible. S6c-architecture-06.title: write_policy_checkpoint in the bindings re-declares the engine's cost-scale default as a bare literal while cobre-sddp exports the named constant the bindings already depend on

The condition at crates/cobre-python/src/policy.rs:507-510 is not an absent config field: it fires only when the caller marked neither the pool nor the producer block, i.e. an absent PROVENANCE MARKER, and the format owner already pins that case - crates/cobre-io/src/output/policy/records.rs:480-482 states that a missing marker is interpreted as scaled-at-1_000_000.0, and rescale_cut_records_for_load (policy_load.rs:83-101) implements exactly that interpretation on load. The module contract at policy.rs:1-9 plus the field doc at policy.rs:104-107 tie the input dicts to what load_policy emits, so an unmarked input is a round-tripped legacy artifact whose bytes sit at the legacy scale; stamping it with 1_000_000.0 is the correct upgrade of an unmarked artifact to a marked one. No engine-side writer reaches any fallback at all: the export path is typed on a plain f64 (crates/cobre-sddp/src/policy/policy_export.rs:642, stamped per pool at :666) and the CLI resolves the factor once from params (crates/cobre-cli/src/commands/broadcast.rs:222), so the site is structurally a bindings-only authoring fallback, not a mirror of the engine default. Consequently the proposed substitution inverts the harm: on the day the config default moves, naming DEFAULT_COST_SCALE_FACTOR here would label legacy-scaled bytes with the new factor and route them through the marked branch that divides by the loading factor (policy_load.rs:88-95), introducing precisely the mis-scaling the candidate wants to prevent, whereas the literal stays correct because the unmarked interpretation is frozen. Nothing is proposed, so no emitted byte moves in either direction; the two constants are equal at this baseline, which is why byteNeutral is n/a.

S6b-test-bloat-06.title: One assertion per subprocess: several integration tests re-run the same invocation to check a second substring of the same output
S6b-test-bloat-06.survivingClaim: Exactly four exit-code-only tests in crates/cobre-cli/tests/cli_validate.rs assert a proper subset of a named sibling's predicates on an identical fixture and identical argv (valid_case_exits_0 under :108-117; missing_buses_json_exits_1 under :131-142 and :144-155; nonexistent_path_exits_2 under :256-264; fpha_hydro_without_production_models_json_fails_validate under :801-812), so their deletion is coverage-neutral by subsumption; the cli_smoke.rs version trio is NOT test-level redundant (only the contains(active_solver_name()) predicate at cli_smoke.rs:66 is dominated) and the residue rests on duplicated fixture-build plus spawn, not on the § Cost discipline link cost, which that rule attributes to the test binary and which expressly prefers more test functions in an existing binary.

S6b-test-bloat-06.argument: The redundancy is real but only in cli_validate.rs, and only as strict predicate subsumption. At the pin valid_case_exits_0 (cli_validate.rs:98-106) asserts success() and nothing else, while valid_case_stdout_contains_buses_count (:108-117) asserts success() plus contains("buses,") on the same make_valid_case fixture and the same argv; missing_buses_json_exits_1 (:119-129) asserts failure().code(1) and is a proper subset of BOTH missing_buses_json_stdout_contains_error (:131-142) and missing_buses_json_stdout_mentions_file (:144-155), and :131-142 is itself a proper subset of validate_failure_report_in_stdout_not_stderr (:207-220); nonexistent_path_exits_2 (:247-254) is a proper subset of nonexistent_path_stderr_mentions_path (:256-264); fpha_hydro_without_production_models_json_fails_validate (:396-406) is a proper subset of fpha_hydro_without_production_models_json_stdout_mentions_file (:801-812), the two sitting four hundred lines apart so neither reader sees the other. A test whose assertion set is a proper subset of a sibling's on an identical fixture and identical argv cannot fail where the sibling passes, so deleting it is coverage-neutral by construction, not by argument. Two parts of the candidate do not survive. First, the cli_smoke.rs version trio is not test-level redundant: version_exits_0_and_contains_version_string (:59-67) chains TWO predicates (CARGO_PKG_VERSION and active_solver_name), version_exits_0_and_stdout_contains_cobre_prefix (:69-76) asserts contains("cobre "), and version_stdout_contains_active_solver (:78-85) asserts the labelled contains("solver: {name}") form; no member is a subset of another, so the candidate's "one substring each" reading is false at the pin and the only dominated item is a single predicate (contains(active_solver_name()) at :66, subsumed by :80-85), not a test. Second, the cost basis is misattributed: .claude/rules/testing.md:113-117 attributes the expensive unit to the integration-test BINARY paying a full C++ solver link, and prescribes adding a test FUNCTION to an existing binary rather than a new file, so extra #[test] functions in an already-linked binary are the shape that rule endorses; a spawn of the built binary pays no link, and nextest runs each #[test] in its own process concurrently, so spawn count is not the rule's cost unit. The residual granularity loss from chaining is real and bounded, since a chained Assert stops at the first failing predicate and reports one failure where the split shape reports several test names; that argues for merging only the strictly-subsumed members rather than collapsing whole families.

S6c-test-bloat-03.title: Four redundant full solver runs pay for preconditions a module-scoped fixture already establishes in the same directory
S6c-test-bloat-03.survivingClaim: Three solver runs are removable, not four, and only one of the two sites reuses an existing fixture: test_boundary_load.py:98 and :124 duplicate the source run at :59 and can be hoisted into a NEWLY authored module-scoped fixture (that module has none today), because the boundary path at run.rs:1299-1310 only reads the source checkpoint; and the bare default Study(...).train() at test_results.py:342 is the single site the already-present module-scoped run_output fixture (:27-37) fully satisfies, since load_stochastic reads only stochastic/*.parquet and the exports.stochastic gate is shared by both entry points at run.rs:1024.
S6c-test-bloat-03.argument: The redundancy is real on both sides, but the title over-counts and mis-attributes the existing pattern, so the claim narrows twice. First, test_boundary_load.py:59, :98 and :124 are the identical call cobre.run.run(VALID_CASE, output_dir=...) with no argument variation beyond the directory name, and all three consume the result read-only: every mutation lands in a separately copied target case (shutil.copytree at :66 and :105, _copy_case_with_renamed_hydro at :130) and each target solve writes to its own output directory (:70, :109, :136). The read-only claim is not merely asserted, it is provable from the code the boundary path runs: apply_training_policy_mode in crates/cobre-python/src/run.rs:1299-1310 resolves the boundary block, calls reconcile_boundary_policy, inject_boundary_cuts into the in-memory StudySetup, and then only writes to stderr; nothing under the boundary source directory is opened for writing. So the source run can be hoisted. But consolidating three identical runs into one fixture removes TWO of them, not three, and the candidate's own reading says three, so the arithmetic that yields the title's four is off by one: the removable population is three, being two in test_boundary_load.py plus one in test_results.py. Second, the phrase about a module-scoped fixture that already establishes the precondition holds only for the test_results.py item. test_boundary_load.py contains no fixture at all, so its consolidation requires authoring a new module-scoped fixture on tmp_path_factory, which is a right-sized change but not a reuse of something present. For the test_results.py item the claim does hold exactly: load_stochastic in crates/cobre-python/src/results.rs:783-798 canonicalizes output_dir and then reads only the two parquet files under stochastic/, so the single precondition is a default-config output tree without stochastic exports, which the module-scoped run_output fixture at test_results.py:27-37 already produces. Switching the entry point from Study.train to cobre.run.run loses nothing, because the exports.stochastic gate is shared: build_study_setup at crates/cobre-python/src/run.rs:933 holds the gate at :1024 and is called by both Study::new_native (crates/cobre-python/src/study.rs:296) and run_via_study (run.rs:1406). Default Study.train entry-point coverage is independently held by test_study.py:101-106 and :216-226, so no claim becomes unwitnessed. One residual cost that the fix shape should keep is the discard at test_boundary_load.py:69 and :108: capfd is function-scoped and the module fixture is set up before it, so the discard becomes belt-and-braces rather than load-bearing, and dropping it would be a separate, unjustified change. No parity suite is touched; test_boundary_load.py and test_results.py are neither of the two CLI-vs-Python parity files nor any of the eleven output-parity files, so the station's tier-1/2 goldens keep asserting exactly what they assert today. The pinned cost-discipline rule is about Rust integration-binary solver link cost and does not speak to pytest fixture scope, so nothing pinned defends the current shape either; the applicable yardstick is the cheapest-tier bullet, cited as a proposal-adjacent standard, not as settled.
